correctness.rationale: For all integers n≥3, column independence and domination are equivalent to isolated zero columns with occupied layers alternating; this proves i(P_n)=2 ceil(n/4) and bijects configurations with rooted binary gap words. Exact cyclic gap-run enumeration proves all cardinality and degree formulas. Adjacent gap swaps give the edge total and a proof of connectivity for 0<h<k by fixing all but a distinguished top token and rotating the distinguished token through all columns. Parity of the gap-index sum is well-defined and flips across every exchange. The enclosed, actually executed direct-bitmask and independent ternary-word checkers corroborate the theorem for n=3..10 and n=3..13 respectively, with additional gap-state checks; finite tests are not misrepresented as the general proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2026 prism dominion theorem is for all minimum dominating sets of size gamma, not independent dominating sets of minimum independent cardinality i. For circumferences divisible by four and congruent to three mod four, its counts partially overlap the vertex enumerator. For the other classes the two problems differ, and no i-graph edges or degrees are determined. Nagy supplies general independent-domination enumerative context, not a prism formula. The 2023 i-graph paper supplies generic adjacency rules but no complete prism classification.

value.rationale: The natural minimum independent-domination feasible space of the cyclic ladder is classified across all circumferences rather than for one arbitrary small graph. It exhibits a sharp periodic freeze/connectivity transition, exact vertex and edge formulas, a full degree-multiplicity law and a bipartition. The graph can have polynomially many configurations but stays of degree at most six, giving structural information relevant to reconfiguration algorithms and combinatorial solution-space geometry. The result cannot be replaced by the easy scalar independence or domination number.
